notation: Logical Arabic in the engine notation (engines.ff6_arabic): a line for each page of the message (the box shows four lines of 220 pixels; the game waits for the button between pages), {line} where a line must end; the encoder breaks the other lines itself, a word at a time, by the glyphs' widths. {Terra}, {Locke}, {Cyan}, {Shadow}, {Edgar}, {Sabin}, {Celes}, {Strago}, {Relm}, {Setzer}, {Mog}, {Gau}, {Gogo} and {Umaro} write a character's name: the entries name.terra to name.umaro give the fourteen names in Arabic, which the hook draws in place of the name the player gave. {center} at a page's start centres its lines (the narration). {Choice} starts a line of a choice and leaves the game's cursor its place at the line's right; {Wait}, {Pause 04}, {Key} and {KeyAfter 04} pass to the game as the English has them, and a translation keeps its original's commands. A message holds Arabic letters, spaces, Western or Arabic-Indic digits and the signs . , : ! - … ، ؛ ؟ « » ( ) ♪ only (the quotes and the brackets are drawn mirrored, as a right-to-left run shows them; ♪ is the opera's note). No vowel marks: the font has none.
